mcqs.question: Before the adoption of the 2022–23 base year, which sequence correctly lists the earlier base years used in India’s GDP series?
mcqs.explanation: The earlier GDP base years were 1948–49, 1960–61, 1970–71, 1980–81, 1993–94, 1999–2000, 2004–05 and 2011–12. The tempting second option reverses the order of 1993–94 and 1999–2000.

mcqs.question:
Match the following items relating to the FY 2026–27 economic outlook with the corresponding details:

List-I
(a) CRISIL forecast and CPI projection
(b) OECD growth forecast
(c) OECD establishment and membership
(d) India–OECD relationship

List-II
(i) 6.1%
(ii) Approximately 7.1%; CPI may rise to 4.3%
(iii) Established on 14 December 1960; 38 members
(iv) India has been a key partner since 2007
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-i, c-iii and d-iv: CRISIL projected approximately 7.1% growth with CPI at 4.3%, while the OECD forecast 6.1%. The OECD was established on 14 December 1960, has 38 members, and India has been a key partner since 2007.

mcqs.question: According to CRISIL’s assessment, what were the approximate reserve-cover periods for India’s strategic petroleum reserves (SPR) and commercial reserves?
options: SPR: approximately 10 days; commercial reserves: approximately 65 days
SPR: approximately 65 days; commercial reserves: approximately 10 days
SPR: approximately 10 days; commercial reserves: approximately 10 days
SPR: approximately 65 days; commercial reserves: approximately 65 days
mcqs.explanation: CRISIL assessed India’s SPR cover at approximately 10 days and commercial reserves at approximately 65 days. The most tempting alternative reverses these two reserve-cover figures.
